headlineHtml: Volumes confirmed, prices whipsawed: record TSMC revenue and power-equipment orders met a CEO shock at Nvidia and the fastest producer-price rise since 2022
ledeLeadHtml: A rebound week that ended on a warning:
ledeHtml: Every major index except Hong Kong and Shanghai rose in the week of 9–13 November, led by Taiwan (+10.0%) and Japan (+6.5%), as earnings confirmed AI data-centre demand in volume terms — record TSMC monthly revenue, record Hon Hai profit, record Applied Materials and Cisco revenue, record Siemens and Japan machine-tool orders. Prices, however, were set by two shocks: Nvidia's founder-CEO resigned mid-week (shares −12.75% on the week) and US producer prices rose +6.5% year on year (前年比), the fastest since November 2022, pushing the US 10-year yield up 29bp to 5.15% and unwinding the semiconductor rotation on Friday.

bullets.leadHtml: Demand was confirmed in volumes, everywhere.
bullets.html: TSMC October revenue was a record NT$586.89bn (+59.7% YoY); Hon Hai Q3 net profit was a record NT$77.5bn (+34%) with AI servers at 54% of sales; Applied Materials Q4 revenue was a record $10.41bn (+53%); Cisco Q1 revenue was a record $18.5bn (+24%) with FY27 guidance raised; SMIC utilisation reached 97.3% on record revenue of $3.19bn.

bullets.leadHtml: Nvidia was the week's price event — governance, not demand.
bullets.html: Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO and director with immediate effect (announced 12 Nov); CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The shares opened −13.1% on 12 Nov, recovered to close −4.34%, and ended the week at $162.85, −12.75% week on week and below a $4tn market cap. Interim management is also reviewing Huang-era financing commitments (the OpenAI Ohio support was reportedly cut from $250bn to $120bn).

bullets.leadHtml: Power and machinery breadth was the second story.
bullets.html: Siemens Q4 orders rose 58% to a record €34.77bn; Hitachi Energy India's orders rose 85.9% with a record backlog of ₹333.35bn and data centres its No. 2 order source; GE Vernova won 765 kV orders (70+ units) from POWERGRID; India approved its first 1,150 kV project (₹68,816 crore); Japan machine-tool orders hit an annual record in ten months (October ¥204.4bn, +42.5% YoY).

bullets.leadHtml: Macro pushed the other way — and won on Friday.
bullets.html: US October CPI was hot (+0.4% MoM vs +0.3% consensus) and PPI rose +6.5% YoY. The US 10-year yield closed at 5.15% (+29bp on the week, its largest weekly rise since April 2025); USD/JPY touched 160.03 and the 10-year JGB yield rose to 2.86%. Friday's US close unwound the rotation: SOX −3.4%, AMD −8.8%, Nvidia −2.0% — yet the SOX still gained +8.05% on the week and all 11 S&P 500 sectors finished higher.

bullets.leadHtml: Capex is still rising; the constraint is delivery and funding cost.
bullets.html: Nebius raised 2026 capex guidance to about $27bn (2027: $40–45bn guided) while some third-party capacity slipped into H1 2027; CoreWeave's backlog reached $132.5bn against $846M of quarterly interest expense; Anthropic's Q3 compute spend was $9.9bn, 58% of revenue; Samsung pulled its HBM packaging plant forward a year to June 2028; China's domestic AI accelerators' combined share passed Nvidia's for the first time (Huawei Ascend 28%).

blocks.heading: 1. Week in numbers — bought: chips ex-Nvidia, Taiwan, Japan, power. Sold: Hong Kong, gold, duration
blocks.html:
Weekly moves, Friday 6 November to Friday 13 November closes (Figure 2). Japan led the developed markets: the Nikkei 225 rose +6.46% to 61,142.35 (+3,707.58 points; its best week in five months) and TOPIX rose +6.30% to 3,941.57 (its best since August 2024) — a rebound from the prior week's rout (Nikkei −9.3% in the week to 6 Nov). Taiwan's TAIEX rose +10.01% (+3,973.48 points to 43,675.12), ending four weekly declines, and Korea's KOSPI rose +4.56% to 5,290.53. In the US, the S&P 500 gained +2.51% to 7,561.67 (best week since early August, snapping a four-week losing streak), the Nasdaq Composite +2.27% to 25,136.27, the Dow +2.07% to 52,347.55, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) +8.05% to 10,146.32 despite Friday's −3.4%. Europe's Euro Stoxx 50 rose +3.19%. The losers were Hong Kong (Hang Seng −3.45%) and Shanghai (−0.41%): the regional split was a China split, not an Asia split.

Rates and FX moved against equities all week. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.152% (+29bp on the week; intraday high 5.17%), the 2-year at about 4.89% (+36bp), as markets priced a possible December Fed hike after hot CPI and PPI prints. USD/JPY closed near 159.7–159.9, having touched 160.03 intraday on Friday — the first breach of 160 since early September — drawing a one-sided-moves warning from Finance Minister Katayama; the dollar index rose about +1.1%. The 10-year JGB yield rose to 2.86% on Friday (+7bp on the day), its highest since 22 October. Commodities: WTI settled at $88.56 (−2.50% on the week) and Brent at $95.84 (−2.52%), a second straight weekly decline as the IEA pointed to a Q4 supply surplus; gold fell about −4.6% to roughly $3,886/oz, its biggest weekly drop in about four months.

What was bought and what was sold (sector rotation, 回転): bought — semiconductors ex-Nvidia (the SOX +8.05% with Nvidia −12.75% means the rest of the index did the work; AMD rose roughly +30% intraw-week before Friday's −8.8%), Taiwan and Japan beta, power equipment and grid names in India (Hitachi Energy India +12% on Friday), and, in the US, breadth itself (all 11 S&P 500 sectors positive on the week; more than 60% of S&P 500 stocks rose even on Friday). Sold — Nvidia specifically, Hong Kong/China exposure, gold and long duration (債券のデュレーション), and on Friday the week's rotation winners (AMD −8.8%, Broadcom −4.8%, Cisco −6.24% despite a beat-and-raise). The pattern is positioning, not fundamentals: the same names were bought on prints early in the week and sold on the discount rate (割引率) by Friday.

blocks.heading: 2. Market performance pack — sectors and coverage movers
blocks.html:
Using the TradingView sector/industry taxonomy as the reference framework: at index level the week's ranking was TAIEX +10.01% > SOX +8.05% > Nikkei +6.46% > TOPIX +6.30% > KOSPI +4.56% > Euro Stoxx 50 +3.19% > S&P 500 +2.51% > Nasdaq +2.27% > Shanghai −0.41% > Hang Seng −3.45% (Figure 2). A full weekly sector matrix by country from TradingView is 未取得 for this edition; the latest-session Japan industry snapshot (Figure 4) shows the tape beneath Friday's flat Tokyo close — electrical products −4.05%, communications equipment −2.36%, electronic components −1.66%, semiconductors −1.06%, against computer hardware +1.68% — i.e. Friday's selling in Japan was also concentrated in the AI complex. In the US on Friday, technology was the worst S&P 500 sector (−1.7%) while the equal-weight index rose, confirming concentration.

Coverage watchlist movers, each tied to its catalyst in Part 3: top — Hitachi Energy India +12% (13 Nov, print + 1,150 kV approval); CoreWeave +24.71% (11 Nov, Q3 beat); the SOX ex-Nvidia complex mid-week (SOX +5.66% on 11 Nov with all 30 constituents up). Bottom — Nvidia −12.75% on the week (CEO resignation); Nebius −16.84% on 12 Nov (capex raise plus capacity slippage, despite a revenue beat); ams OSRAM −9.2% on Friday (Q4 guidance below consensus); SoftBank Group −5.11% on 13 Nov in Tokyo (follow-through from its H1 loss on the US AIDC power-procurement write-down); Cisco −6.24% on Friday despite record results — the clearest sign that by Friday the discount rate, not the print, was setting prices.

blocks.heading: 3a. Semiconductors and AIDC — record volumes, a governance shock, rising capex
blocks.html:
Semiconductors. TSMC's October revenue of NT$586.89bn (+59.7% YoY, +14.7% MoM) was its largest month on record (previous record: August, NT$514.81bn); January–October revenue reached NT$4,485.62bn (+43.3%). Its board also approved appropriations of $40.93bn and up to $500M each of investment linked to Anthropic and OpenAI (noon packet, 11 Nov). Applied Materials posted record Q4 revenue of $10.41bn (+53% YoY), adjusted EPS of $4.16 vs $4.06 consensus, and Q1 FY27 guidance of $11.1bn ± $0.5bn vs $10.89bn consensus; management guided to 2027 wafer-fab equipment (WFE) demand growth of more than +30%. SMIC's Q3 revenue was a record $3.19bn (+33.9% YoY) with utilisation of 97.3% and gross margin of 29.9% vs 26–28% guidance; Q4 guidance is revenue +4–6% QoQ. GlobalFoundries' Q3 gross margin was a record 31.4% (+540bp YoY) on revenue of $1.899bn, with communications infrastructure & data centre revenue +81% YoY; its 2026 silicon-photonics revenue outlook was raised to $500M, and it broke ground on the first Malta fab under the US–Japan initiative (up to $21bn of Japanese funding; first fab about $10bn, 2029 start, roughly 900k 300mm wafers a year). In Japan, Micronics Japan's nine-month operating profit rose +138.9% YoY to ¥26.99bn with the FY operating-profit guide raised to ¥36.1bn and the dividend lifted to ¥208; Eblen's H1 operating profit rose +106.2% to ¥490m on HBM-related demand, with FY guides raised sharply — the HBM investment chain is reaching probe cards and measurement/control equipment. The counter-example was SUMCO: nine-month sales +9.2% to ¥332.5bn but an operating loss of ¥4.40bn — volume without price. Resonac raised its FY core operating-profit guide to ¥250bn (from ¥196bn) on semiconductor materials, while selling its graphite-electrode business to Aurelius and booking a roughly ¥105bn non-recurring loss — portfolio concentration on chip materials, at a stated price. Nippon Steel Chemical & Material guided AI-server substrate resin volumes +80% and bonding-wire volumes +15% for FY2026.

AIDC. CoreWeave's Q3 revenue was $3.661bn (+168% YoY vs $3.54bn consensus), backlog $132.5bn (from $104.2bn at Q2-end), adjusted EBITDA margin 62%, active power above 1.7GW — against a net loss of $709M and interest expense of $846M; FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $13.0–13.3bn. Nebius' Q3 revenue was $980.8M (+571% YoY vs $907.5M consensus), but about $325M was asset-light partner revenue of a temporary nature, some third-party capacity slipped into H1 2027, the $7–9bn ARR target moved from December to February 2027, and 2026 capex guidance rose to about $27bn (from $20–25bn), with an initial 2027 view of $40–45bn capex on $12–13bn revenue. Hon Hai's Q3 net profit was a record NT$77.52bn (+34% YoY vs NT$69.6bn consensus) on revenue of NT$3.02tn (+46%), with cloud & networking (AI servers) at 54% of sales and gross margin of 6.02%; Pegatron's October revenue rose +59.6% YoY to NT$188.08bn and Wistron's Q3 net profit rose +149% (held item, noon packet 12 Nov). Cisco's record Q1 revenue of $18.5bn (+24%) and FY27 guide raise (to $74.8–75.8bn, with hyperscaler AI-infrastructure revenue seen at about $9bn, more than double FY26) show capex broadening from GPUs to networking. Cerebras posted record core revenue of $230.9M (+70%), a first adjusted net profit of about $30M, 700MW of contracted capacity and RPO (remaining performance obligations, 残存履行義務) of $26.1bn, with Microsoft its third hyperscaler customer. Anthropic's amended S-1 showed Q3 revenue of $16.96bn with compute/infrastructure spend of $9.9bn (58% of revenue, up from 48% in Q2) and purchase/lease commitments of about $895.4bn. Naver disclosed a roughly ₩2tn, five-year, ~20MW inference-compute contract and an AI-factory ramp of 55MW (H1 2027) → 100MW (end-2027) → 200MW (2028), with secured capacity already above its 2028 disclosure target. SoftBank Group's H1 net loss of ¥768.0bn (vs a ¥2,924.1bn profit a year earlier) was driven by a ¥597.2bn loss on revising US AIDC power-equipment procurement and ¥270.1bn of Intel/derivative losses — execution risk in the AIDC build-out, in print. Weekend follow-ups (15 Nov packets): Digital Realty plans a further $10bn of investment in Japanese data centres; TI Korea flagged the AI bottleneck spreading to mature-node power and embedded chips; Atlanta Electricals reported new transformer orders.

blocks.heading: 3b. Power, cooling, machinery, components and humanoids
blocks.html:
Power. Siemens' Q4 industrial profit was a record €3.89bn (+22% vs €3.71bn company consensus) on revenue of €23.68bn (+11%) and record orders of €34.77bn (+58%), led by mobility and smart infrastructure including data-centre electrical equipment; its medium-term revenue growth target was raised from 6–9% to 7–11%. Hitachi Energy India's Q2 (Jul–Sep) revenue rose +63.6% to ₹2,996.5 crore with orders of ₹4,120.8 crore (+85.9%) — grid transmission (transformers, STATCOM, cooling, AIS/GIS) led, data centres were the No. 2 order source, exports rose +41% in the quarter (+184% in H1) — and backlog reached a record ₹33,335.4 crore, about 11.1x one quarter's revenue. GE Vernova won POWERGRID orders for 70+ 765 kV transformers and shunt reactors (deliveries 2026 to end-2027; value undisclosed, 未取得). India's National Committee on Transmission approved the country's first 1,150 kV project (Raigarh–Kotra–Rourkela–Kolaghat; ₹68,816 crore, about six years, for 12GW of renewables plus storage) — Hitachi Energy is India's only type-tested 1,150 kV transformer maker, per Equirus via the Economic Times. CG Power won a ₹9bn order to supply transformers from India for a US hyperscale data centre (12–20 months execution). Korea's Honam chip cluster added transformer orders with 4GW planned by 2029. On the theme layer: Infineon will supply the first 900V GaN bidirectional switch to Enphase for its IQ solid-state transformer (固態変圧器) for AI data centres — device testing complete, integration under way, qualification to follow — direct evidence for the solid-state-transformer and GaN themes in this report's coverage. Cooling: Samsung Electronics was reported (CLS, 13 Nov) to be in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing (market cap about $5.6bn; shares down about 15% since its 3 Nov print) — a possible deal within weeks, with Daikin, LG Electronics and Vertiv also investing in the same bottleneck.

Machinery, FA and components. Japan's October machine-tool orders were ¥204.4bn (+42.5% YoY; domestic ¥52.3bn, +46.5%; foreign ¥152.1bn, +41.1%), the second-highest month on record, taking January–October orders to ¥1,873.7bn — above the 2018 full-year record of ¥1,815.8bn with two months to spare; order backlog at end-September was ¥1,098.2bn. JMTBA's chairman named AI/data centres, semiconductor equipment, energy and aerospace as the drivers — explicitly not autos, unlike 2018. Daifuku raised FY guides (sales ¥770bn, operating profit ¥119bn) and its order range to ¥970bn–¥1tn, with a ¥40bn buyback. Amada raised its FY3/2027 net profit forecast to ¥40.0bn (+31% YoY, above the ¥39.7bn QUICK consensus) on AI data-centre sheet-metal demand. SMC raised its full-year ordinary-profit forecast by +36.0% to above consensus, with a buyback of up to ¥50bn. THK raised its FY12/2026 net profit forecast to ¥58.8bn, with revenue of ¥320bn (+33% YoY) and operating profit of ¥52bn (3.6x). Takasago Thermal raised its FY3/2027 operating-profit forecast by +20% to ¥60bn and its orders forecast to ¥620bn — above ¥600bn for the first time — on semiconductor-plant renewal and data-centre work, though H1 operating profit fell −26.7%, leaving ¥41.9bn to be earned in H2 (a back-loaded plan to test). Ebara's Q3 operating profit rose +69% (held item, 13 Nov night packet). Humanoids: ASUS unveiled its first humanoid, Gallop (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor; learning packaging work in group EMS factories; customer pilots 2027, market launch H2 2028; price and volumes 未取得); Schaeffler's Taicang lighthouse factory holds humanoid orders of about €400M (held item, 12 Nov noon packet); JPMorgan published a 2030 humanoid outlook (held item, 12 Nov night packet). The Japan read-through remains the component names — Harmonic Drive, Nabtesco, THK — with THK's revision this week the only hard number in the bucket.

blocks.heading: 4. Statistics tracker — the fixed panel, read as trends
blocks.html: The fixed panel (Figure 6) reads this week as one connected story across its four blocks. Capex: guidance is still being raised, not cut — Nebius 2026 capex to about $27bn with a $40–45bn 2027 view, CoreWeave backlog $132.5bn, Cisco's hyperscaler AI-infrastructure revenue view doubled to about $9bn, Naver's secured AI-factory capacity already above its 2028 target — while the funding side tightened in the same week (US 10-year at 5.15%; CoreWeave quarterly interest of $846M against $3.66bn of revenue). Anchor-company orders and backlog: Siemens orders +58%, Hitachi Energy India backlog at a record (about 11.1x quarterly revenue), Japan machine-tool backlog ¥1,098.2bn, Daifuku's order range raised to up to ¥1tn. Trade and country statistics: the week's hard releases were prices, not volumes — US CPI +0.4% MoM (core +0.3%, a third straight +0.3%, about +3.6% annualised; the YoY print was not published because the shutdown left October 2025 data uncollected) and PPI +6.5% YoY with goods +10.2% YoY. Japan machinery orders (September) and October trade are due next week (19 and 18 Nov) and will be scored in the next edition; JMTBA orders (above) are the freshest Japan capex-volume print. Shipments and demand: TSMC's record month and SMIC's 97.3% utilisation say foundry demand is supply-bound into 2027 (SMIC's co-CEO: AI-related supply constraints persist through 2027); China's domestic accelerators shipped more units than Nvidia in China for the first time (Huawei Ascend above 570k units, 28% share) as export controls bite — Bessent said on 13 Nov that he had himself argued Megaspeed should be added to the Entity List, with a House closed-door briefing requested for 18 Nov. Korea concentration is the panel's risk marker: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix margin balances totalled ₩6.9669tn as of 12 Nov — 27.2% of all KOSPI+KOSDAQ margin loans and 36.5% of KOSPI-only margin loans (FnGuide via BigGo, 15 Nov noon packet). Transformer lead times: no new headline number this week (未取得); the order flow (CG Power 12–20 months execution; GE Vernova deliveries into end-2027) is consistent with the standing 128-week reference from the 11 Nov deep-dive. Data-centre capacity additions: Naver 55MW → 200MW (2027–28), SpaceX's Memphis campus reportedly to 2.4GW (SemiAnalysis via 15 Nov morning packet), Cerebras 700MW contracted, Digital Realty a further $10bn for Japan.

blocks.heading: Part 3 — Catalysts and the week ahead
5. Catalyst attribution — why it moved, why it happened
blocks.html: Figure 7 lists the events that actually drove the week's performance. Two mechanisms matter. First, the largest single-stock move (Nvidia, −12.75% on the week) was a governance event, not a demand event: reporting on 12 Nov that the board was considering removing the founder became, the same day, a confirmed immediate resignation after a board investigation, with no designated successor and the CFO doubling as interim CEO — the price fell on succession and commitment uncertainty (including the review of Huang-era financing deals), not on any change to orders, and the quarter being reported next week closed on 25 October, before he left. Second, the sector-level moves were expectation trades on the discount rate: hot CPI (10 Nov) set the headwind, record prints (TSMC, CoreWeave) drove the mid-week rotation into everything-but-Nvidia (SOX +5.66% on 11 Nov), and hot PPI (13 Nov) plus a 5.15% 10-year yield unwound it on Friday — including in names that had just beaten (Cisco −6.24%). Positioning amplified both legs: Korea's ₩6.97tn two-stock margin concentration is the regional marker of the same crowding.

blocks.heading: 6. Week ahead — 16 to 22 November (times in JST)
blocks.html: Monday 16 Nov, 08:50 — Japan Q3 GDP, first estimate: the split between domestic demand and capex is the read, ahead of the BOJ's December meeting (17–18 Dec) with USD/JPY at 160 and the 10-year JGB at 2.86%. Tuesday 17 Nov (US) — US October retail sales; Wednesday 18 Nov, 06:20 — Nvidia Q3 results (about 16:20 ET), call at 07:00 JST (17:00 ET): guidance form under the interim CEO matters as much as the print (company outlook $108.0bn ±2%; consensus about $108.9bn). Wednesday 18 Nov — Japan October trade statistics and visitor arrivals; the requested closed-door House briefing on the Huang matter; Anthropic IPO pricing (evening ET; range $70–78, ticker ANT). Thursday 19 Nov — Japan September machinery orders (the test for Candidate 3); Anthropic's first Nasdaq trading day; FOMC minutes (early JST); Walmart Q3 (US, before the open). Friday 20 Nov — Japan October national CPI. Each maps to a tracker in Figure 6; next week's edition will score them against the expectations recorded here.
